title: Understanding the Pattern
text: The pattern .*:[A-Za-z\d]+(,[A-Za-z\d]+)* is designed to match strings that start with any characters, followed by a colon, and then a sequence of alphanumeric characters separated by commas.

title: Analyzing the Match All Cases
text:
Let's break down the 'Match all of these below' cases:
$$1$$. "total cats petted: 60,102,305"
$$2$$. "my cats' names are: amy,baron,carol"
$$3$$. "the current time is 20:59"

Consider how the pattern .*:[A-Za-z\d]+(,[A-Za-z\d]+)* applies to each of these cases.

title: Analyzing the Match None Cases
text: Now, let's consider why the pattern should not match the 'Match none of these below' cases. Think about what makes these cases different from the 'Match all' cases.

title: Pattern Breakdown
text:
The pattern .*:[A-Za-z\d]+(,[A-Za-z\d]+)* can be broken down as follows:
- .*: Matches any character (except for a newline) zero or more times, followed by a colon.
- [A-Za-z\d]+: Matches one or more alphanumeric characters.
- (,[A-Za-z\d]+)*: Matches zero or more sequences of a comma followed by one or more alphanumeric characters.

Does this pattern fully match all the 'Match all' cases?
